target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : ArithmeticTheory) [T.Δ₁], Def3 T → Def3 (T ∪ T.localReflectionOn Set.univ).theory
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is the proposition that for every arithmetic axiom set T equipped with a Δ₁ definition of its axioms, if every member of T is true in the standard natural numbers, then every sentence derivable from T together with all instances of local reflection for T is true in the standard natural numbers. The added instances are Prov_T(⌜σ⌝) → σ for every arithmetic sentence σ, whether or not T proves σ; the provability predicate is for T, not for the enlarged theory. T need not be deductively closed or extend any specified base theory."}
translation: Target is the proposition that for every arithmetic axiom set T equipped with a Δ₁ definition of its axioms, if every member of T is true in the standard natural numbers, then every sentence derivable from T together with all instances of local reflection for T is true in the standard natural numbers. The added instances are Prov_T(⌜σ⌝) → σ for every arithmetic sentence σ, whether or not T proves σ; the provability predicate is for T, not for the enlarged theory. T need not be deductively closed or extend any specified base theory.

divergences.description: The Lean statement specializes the parenthetical to first-order arithmetic with truth in the standard natural numbers, and requires a Δ₁ presentation of T to define its provability predicate. The parenthetical itself imposes no such presentation requirement.

Rather than adding one true sentence, the target adds the whole local reflection scheme for T. This is a valid application of the parenthetical: if T's axioms are true, every theorem of T is true, so each instance Prov_T(⌜σ⌝) → σ is true and adding them all preserves soundness.

judgement.summary: The target captures the intended contrast: the enlarged theory asserts reflection for the original T, not for the enlarged theory itself. It is an application of Chalmers's parenthetical, not a formalization of his particular “I am F” extension.
